title: MTD for Jointly Owned Rental Property: What Each Owner Should Check
excerpt: If you own a rental property with someone else, do not assume one person’s MTD arrangement automatically deals with both owners. Each person’s tax position and relevant share need checking.
metaTitle: Joint Rental Property and MTD: Check Each Owner | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check MTD for jointly owned rental property using each owner's share, other qualifying income and the records needed for quarterly reporting.
featuredImageAlt: Two joint property owners each hold their own share-of-rent folder while an adviser checks ownership records.

sources.label: GOV.UK — PIM1035 - Introduction: Jointly owned property and partnerships - HMRC internal manual
GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Send quarterly updates - Guidance

content:
If you own a rental property with someone else, do not assume one person’s MTD arrangement automatically deals with both owners. Each person’s tax position and relevant share need checking.

Start with the ownership information

Tell your accountant who owns the property, how it is held and how rental income has been reported. Different rules can apply to spouses or civil partners and other joint owners. Do not choose a split simply because it produces the smallest bill.

Bring the ownership documents and any relevant declaration or agreement. A bank account receiving all the rent does not, on its own, establish the tax treatment.

Keep the full statements available

Give the accountant the total property statement and explain the share attributed to you. Avoid sending only a personally calculated net amount with no supporting breakdown. This helps the accountant reconcile letting-agent deductions and shared costs.

HMRC provides specific quarterly-reporting options for jointly let property. Your accountant should decide how those rules apply and what still needs completing before the annual return.

Agree who handles which owner

Ask whether the engagement covers you alone or includes a separate service for the other owner. Keep authorisations and approvals clear for each person.

Example: one statement, two owners

A letting agent may issue a statement showing the whole property’s rent. Your accountant needs to identify the relevant share rather than placing the full amount on both owners’ records. Keep the complete statement so deductions and allocations can be reconciled.

Does my co-owner’s MTD status decide mine?

Not by itself. Each person’s qualifying income and circumstances need consideration. Explain any other trades or properties you hold as well as the jointly owned property.

Can I change the split during onboarding?

Do not change the declared share simply to reach a preferred result. Ownership, the relationship between owners and relevant evidence affect the treatment. If the underlying arrangement has changed, give the accountant the documents and dates before records are updated.

Next step: Share the ownership details and existing rental statements with TaxSimba before assuming the package covers every owner or property.

Put it into practice

Two owners can have different MTD start dates

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A jointly owned property has £28,000 gross annual rent, shared equally. Each owner starts with their own £14,000 share for the relevant qualifying-income check. One also has £25,000 gross self-employment income; the other has PAYE salary. Their MTD positions can differ because the eligible sources differ. They give the accountant the ownership evidence and complete agent statements, then confirm who reports which figures. The property's full rent is not entered as each person's income.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
What is each person's reportable share?Keep the ownership and income-allocation evidence rather than splitting from memory.
Does each owner have other qualifying income?Assess each individual's relevant trades and property sources for the correct year.
What quarterly reporting choice is being used?Confirm the permitted joint-property approach and how any deferred expenses will be completed at year-end.

Two more questions you may have

Does one owner's MTD duty automatically cover the other?

No. Each person has their own tax position and any required reporting. A shared agent statement is not a shared personal tax return.

Can we both report the full rent then split the tax?

No. Establish the correct share of income and costs for each return before calculating the liability.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • List all owners and ownership evidence.
  • Record each owner's gross income share.
  • Check other qualifying income separately.
  • Agree quarterly reporting and expense completion.
  • Keep separate submission references for each person.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: CIS Subcontractors and MTD: Gross Income Is Not Your Bank Receipt
excerpt: CIS deductions and MTD reporting answer different questions. A deduction is an advance payment towards tax; it should not simply disappear because your bank receives a smaller amount.
metaTitle: CIS and MTD: Use Gross Income, Not the Bank Payout | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check MTD qualifying income for CIS subcontractors using gross trading receipts before CIS deductions and expenses, with statements to support the totals.
featuredImageAlt: A subcontractor compares a large gross invoice with a smaller bank receipt and a separate CIS deduction statement.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Construction Industry Scheme (CIS)
GOV.UK — What you must do as a Construction Industry Scheme (CIS) subcontractor: Get paid
GOV.UK — Work out your qualifying income for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax

content:
CIS deductions and MTD reporting answer different questions. A deduction is an advance payment towards tax; it should not simply disappear because your bank receives a smaller amount.

Start with the payment statement

Keep the contractor’s payment and deduction statements alongside your invoices and bank records. Explain what was paid, what was deducted and whether materials or other amounts need separate consideration. Your accountant needs the underlying figures rather than only the net deposit.

For example, £1,000 of relevant income with a £200 CIS deduction can leave £800 arriving in the bank. Recording only £800 as income would not describe the original transaction properly. This simplified example is not a universal calculation for every invoice, especially where VAT or materials are involved.

Keep eligibility separate from the final bill

MTD qualifying income concerns relevant gross receipts, not the money left after tax deductions or business expenses. The accountant also needs to reconcile CIS tax already paid when completing the annual position. Do not deduct it again as an ordinary business running cost.

Tell the accountant about other work

Private jobs, another trade or rental income can affect the overall review. CIS status alone does not establish whether you need MTD.

A useful reconciliation check

For each contractor, compare the invoice, payment statement and bank receipt. Where the amounts differ, identify tax deductions, materials or other adjustments rather than forcing the figures to match by deleting the difference.

Is CIS tax deducted an ordinary expense?

No. It is tax paid in advance, not simply a cost of buying materials or running the business. Keep it identifiable so the accountant can review the credit against the final position.

Do contractors and subcontractors have the same obligations?

No. A contractor’s responsibilities for paying subcontractors are different from a sole-trader subcontractor’s own Income Tax work. If you do both, tell the accountant. An MTD service should not be assumed to include monthly contractor CIS returns unless that work is expressly agreed.

Next step: Share the contractor statements and full income records with TaxSimba so the bookkeeping and tax deductions can be reconciled within the agreed service.

Put it into practice

CIS withheld is still part of gross receipts

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A subcontractor's relevant annual receipts are £38,000 before £7,600 CIS deductions, leaving £30,400 paid after CIS. He uses the gross figure when checking MTD qualifying income for the appropriate look-back year, adding any other relevant trading or property income. He does not use the smaller bank total or subtract tools and travel for that test. The £7,600 is separately tracked for tax credit on the annual return, with contractor statements retained.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Have CIS deductions reduced the income total?Reconcile gross receipts before withholding rather than using net bank payments.
Are material reimbursements and other receipts captured?Check the full trading-income records and the correct tax treatment of each amount.
Which threshold year applies?Use the published look-back year and start date, not a current monthly payout.

Two more questions you may have

Do CIS deductions mean my reporting is already digital?

No. CIS withholding and MTD record and update duties are separate systems. Check whether both apply.

Can business costs bring gross income below the MTD threshold?

Expenses affect profit, but the qualifying-income test starts before expenses and CIS deductions.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Collect all contractor statements.
  • Reconcile gross receipts to net payments and deductions.
  • Add other relevant business or property income.
  • Identify the correct look-back tax year.
  • Check MTD scope and keep CIS credits separate.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Bank Feeds and MTD: Why Connected Does Not Mean Complete
excerpt: Connecting a bank account can help collect information, but it is not proof that your books are complete. Your accountant still needs to understand the transactions and identify anything outside the connection.
metaTitle: MTD Bank Feeds: Check Your Records Are Complete | TaxSimba
metaDescription: A connected bank feed is only part of MTD bookkeeping. Check cash, platform deductions, private transfers and missing transactions before updates.
featuredImageAlt: A shopkeeper connects a bank feed but adds cash-sale records and receipts from another account, not complete automatically.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Create digital records - Guidance
GOV.UK — Business records if you're self-employed: What records to keep

content:
Connecting a bank account can help collect information, but it is not proof that your books are complete. Your accountant still needs to understand the transactions and identify anything outside the connection.

List what the feed cannot explain

A bank entry may not show the business purpose, a split between private and business use, or the detail behind a payment-platform payout. Cash receipts and transactions in another account may also need separate records.

Keep supporting documents available. HMRC’s digital-record guidance does not remove the need for relevant invoices, statements and other evidence.

Check the period covered

Tell the accountant if an account was opened, closed or reconnected during the year. Download missing statements and identify gaps. Avoid assuming a refreshed connection has automatically imported every earlier transaction.

Look for duplicates as well as omissions

An imported transaction, a manual entry and a payment-platform record may describe the same underlying event. Explain transfers and provide platform summaries so the accountant can reconcile the records rather than adding every visible amount together.

Agree who checks the result

Ask what you should upload, what the accountant maintains and how queries are resolved. Do not mark the bookkeeping complete simply because the dashboard says an account is connected.

Example: a platform payout

A customer payment processed through a platform can reach the bank after fees have been deducted. The bank feed may show the deposit but not the original sale and fee breakdown. The platform statement helps the accountant reconcile the difference.

Is every bank-feed item a business transaction?

No. A feed can include personal spending, transfers, refunds and money introduced by the owner. Those need identifying instead of treating every incoming amount as sales and every outgoing amount as a deductible expense.

Can I stop keeping invoices after connecting the bank?

No. Retain the relevant supporting evidence. A transaction description is not always enough to establish what was purchased, why it was for business or whether it was included elsewhere. Ask which documents the accountant needs and keep the process consistent.

Next step: Tell TaxSimba which accounts and platforms you use, and provide the supporting records requested by the assigned accountant.

Put it into practice

Connected does not mean reconciled

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A shop's bank feed imports a £470 platform payout and a £1,000 transfer from the owner's savings. The platform statement shows £500 sales and £30 fees; the £1,000 is funding, not a customer sale. Cash sales are outside the feed entirely. Before an MTD update, the owner reconciles these sources and classifies the entries. A green connection indicator confirms access to a feed, not that income, expenses or reporting are complete.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
What activity never reaches this feed?List cash, other accounts and platform records to avoid gaps.
Are payouts already net of fees?Use statements to identify gross receipts and separate deductions.
Are transfers or duplicates treated as sales?Reconcile and label them before relying on software totals.

Two more questions you may have

Can I accept every suggested category?

Review it against the transaction's purpose and supporting record. Automatic suggestions can be wrong or incomplete.

Does connecting a feed send an update to HMRC?

No. Record import, reconciliation and submission are separate steps. Keep the acknowledgement for the actual update.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • List all banks, platforms and cash sources.
  • Check feed dates and missing periods.
  • Reconcile gross sales, fees and payouts.
  • Label transfers, refunds and duplicates.
  • Confirm records are reviewed before submission.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: My Income Has Fallen: Can I Stop Using MTD?
excerpt: A quieter trading year does not automatically switch off MTD. Once you are in the service, the rules for leaving need checking separately from the original eligibility test.
metaTitle: Income Fallen: Can You Stop Using MTD? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Falling income does not automatically end MTD. Check qualifying-income history, ceased sources and HMRC's opt-out or exemption rules before stopping.
featuredImageAlt: A trader with falling income checks several consecutive tax-year folders with adviser before deciding obligations.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Work out your qualifying income for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Add or cease income sources - Guidance

content:
A quieter trading year does not automatically switch off MTD. Once you are in the service, the rules for leaving need checking separately from the original eligibility test.

Explain why the income changed

Tell your accountant whether sales fell, a property was sold, a trade stopped or an earlier return was wrong. These are different situations. A lower bank balance does not necessarily mean lower qualifying income.

HMRC’s guidance says that after starting MTD, qualifying income below the relevant threshold for three tax years in a row can allow you to choose to opt out. Corrections to a previous return or the cessation of income sources can require a different assessment.

Keep the records while the position is checked

Do not simply stop answering record requests or abandon upcoming obligations. Ask the accountant to confirm what remains due and what needs notifying to HMRC. Keep any confirmation of a changed position.

Separate the service contract from HMRC obligations

Cancelling a subscription is not the same as leaving MTD. Likewise, a dashboard change does not establish that HMRC has accepted an opt-out. Check both the tax position and the contractual arrangement.

Example: one lower year

If a business has a single year below a headline threshold, do not assume its existing MTD obligations have ended. Ask which exit rule applies to the person’s history and circumstances. A corrected prior-year return is also different from a genuine fall in current trading income.

What if one business stops but another continues?

Give the accountant the complete picture. Stopping one income source is not the same as ceasing all relevant self-employment and property income. Record cessation dates and any money received afterwards.

What evidence should I keep?

Retain the returns, income records and HMRC correspondence used to assess the change. Ask for a clear explanation of what remains due. Keep that explanation with the service records, rather than relying on a phone conversation or the disappearance of a reminder.

Next step: Give TaxSimba the relevant returns, current records and details of any stopped activity so the accountant can assess the correct next step.

Put it into practice

One quiet year is not an automatic exit

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A designer already in MTD has a much quieter year and expects lower gross receipts. He gathers the relevant return history and distinguishes an ongoing business from permanent cessation. He checks the current HMRC rules before changing the reporting routine and retains any confirmation. He does not stop sending required updates merely because one quarter has no sales. Lower advance tax payments may be a separate issue to review using a supported liability estimate.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Has income fallen or has the source ceased?Record the actual change and dates; the reporting consequences can differ.
What qualifying-income history is relevant?Use the required consecutive-year evidence under current HMRC rules.
Has an exit or exemption been confirmed?Follow the official route and keep meeting existing obligations until the applicable position is clear.

Two more questions you may have

Is one year below the entry threshold enough?

Do not assume so. Entry thresholds and leaving conditions differ; check the current rule and the required income history.

Does a lower tax bill mean I can leave MTD?

No. Tax liability and gross qualifying-income conditions are different tests. Check each separately.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Record gross qualifying income by tax year.
  • List continuing and ceased sources.
  • Keep cessation or changed-circumstance evidence.
  • Check the current leaving or exemption route.
  • Retain confirmation and agree any final submissions.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Self-Employed Hairdressers and Beauty Professionals: Tax Return Preparation
excerpt: Salon work can involve employment, self-employment or a mixture of arrangements. Before preparing a tax return, make sure the accountant understands how you actually work.
metaTitle: Hairdresser and Beauty Tax Returns: Records to Prepare | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare self-employed hairdresser and beauty records: cash, card and platform income, chair rent, products, mixed costs and employment-status details.
featuredImageAlt: A self-employed hairdresser sorts salon chair-rent receipts, client payments and product stock records at a desk.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Check employment status if you work in hair and beauty
GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Overview
GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Office, property and equipment

content:
Salon work can involve employment, self-employment or a mixture of arrangements. Before preparing a tax return, make sure the accountant understands how you actually work.

Explain the working arrangement

Describe whether you rent a chair or room, set your own prices, take bookings directly and buy your own supplies. A contract label alone does not settle employment status. HMRC has specific guidance for people working in hair and beauty.

If you are employed by a salon and see private clients separately, give the accountant both sets of records. Keep employment documents separate from the business takings.

Capture every payment method

Maintain a consistent record of cash, card and bank payments. Include booking-platform summaries and relevant deductions so the accountant can reconcile the totals. Mark transfers and personal contributions clearly.

Keep expense evidence useful

Organise supply invoices, chair or room-rental statements and other business costs. Explain mixed use of a phone or workspace. Ordinary personal spending should not be relabelled as business spending just because appearance matters in the industry.

Make a note of cancelled appointments, refunds and adjustments rather than changing totals without explanation. The trail should help someone else understand the figures.

Example: salon employment and private clients

A person employed for part of the week may also operate a separate mobile service. The accountant needs the employment documents and private-client records. Do not mix the salary with cash takings and describe the whole amount as salon turnover.

Are cash tips and card receipts irrelevant if they are small?

Give the accountant the complete payment information rather than excluding amounts yourself. Explain what the receipts relate to so the correct treatment can be assessed.

Are ordinary clothes and grooming automatically business expenses?

No. Personal appearance being important to the work does not make every related cost deductible. Organise protective clothing, uniforms and other specific costs for review, keeping personal spending separate. Ask about the actual item and use instead of relying on a broad industry expense list.

Next step: Tell TaxSimba how your salon or mobile service operates and provide a sample of your records. The accountant can then confirm what information is needed and whether the selected service is suitable.

Put it into practice

Chair rent and card fees need their own trail

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A self-employed stylist receives £520 through a card platform after £15 fees and also takes £180 cash. She supplies the £535 gross card sales, fee statement and cash record. Chair rent and product purchases sit in the expense pack with invoices. She tells the accountant whether she sets prices, manages clients and works elsewhere, since a salon arrangement's label alone does not settle employment status. Personal treatments and ordinary clothing are not folded into product costs.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Are all client receipts recorded?Reconcile cash, card, booking-platform and tip records without counting payouts twice.
What does the salon arrangement actually involve?Provide the agreement and working facts for any employment-status question.
Are private costs separated?Mark personal products, ordinary clothing and mixed-use costs for review.

Two more questions you may have

Can I report only what the booking platform pays out?

Check whether fees or refunds were deducted. Keep the gross sales report and reconcile it to the net bank payout.

Does renting a chair automatically prove self-employment?

No. The real working relationship matters. Keep the agreement and explain control, clients and financial arrangements.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Collect booking, cash, card and tip records.
  • Reconcile platform fees and payouts.
  • Gather chair-rent and business product invoices.
  • Identify personal and mixed-use costs.
  • Provide working arrangements and other-income documents.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Company Directors: Your Personal Tax Return Is Different from Company Filing
excerpt: A company’s accounts and Corporation Tax return are separate from a director’s personal tax position. Completing one does not automatically complete the other.
metaTitle: Company Director Personal Tax Return: What to Prepare | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Separate a director’s personal tax return from company filings. Gather salary, dividends, benefits, other income and the reason Self Assessment is needed.
featuredImageAlt: A company director separates company accounts and personal salary/dividend papers into different folders.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Director information hub: Self Assessment for directors
GOV.UK — Check if you need to send a Self Assessment tax return

content:
A company’s accounts and Corporation Tax return are separate from a director’s personal tax position. Completing one does not automatically complete the other.

Check whether a personal return is needed

Being a director does not, by itself, settle every filing question. HMRC’s current director guidance explains that salary, dividends and other untaxed income need considering. Use the current Self Assessment checker and deal with any notice to file.

Tell the accountant about employment income, dividends, benefits and income outside the company. Do not rely only on the money transferred from the company bank account.

Gather the personal evidence

Provide the relevant employment documents, dividend records and information about other income. Explain any payments you do not understand rather than labelling every transfer as salary or a dividend yourself.

Ask the person preparing company records for the information needed for the personal return. Keep the tax year distinct from the company’s accounting period.

Confirm the purchased service

An individual SA package should not be assumed to include company accounts, Corporation Tax, payroll or work on directors’ loans. These need an explicit scope check before purchase.

Example: one company, two different returns

The company’s accounting period might end in December while the director’s personal tax year ends on 5 April. Documents need to be allocated to the relevant return; the company-year end is not automatically the cut-off for every personal figure.

Is every company withdrawal a dividend?

No. A transfer can have a different explanation, and distributions need appropriate records. Ask the accountant responsible for the company records to clarify the treatment rather than naming the payment after the event to suit the tax return.

Does MTD automatically apply to a director’s salary and dividends?

Do not infer MTD eligibility from the directorship alone. Relevant sole-trader or property income needs its own check. Personal Self Assessment, company filing and MTD eligibility are related administrative questions but are not interchangeable.

Next step: Tell TaxSimba you are a director and describe the personal income needing review. Ask separately about any company work, rather than assuming it is included.

Put it into practice

Company filing does not complete the director's return

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A director has a P60, dividend vouchers and taxable benefits information. Her company has filed its accounts, but that does not report all of her personal income. She checks whether a personal return is required and supplies the relevant documents with savings, property and pension details. She also flags any payments described as director loans rather than assuming they are salary or dividends. The personal and company records must reconcile without treating them as the same filing.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Why is a personal return required?Check the individual's income and HMRC notice; directorship alone is not a universal filing trigger.
Are salary and dividends evidenced?Use payroll records and dividend documentation, not just personal bank credits.
Are there benefits or loan transactions?Provide the relevant records so their tax treatment can be checked.

Two more questions you may have

Does Corporation Tax filing cover my personal tax?

No. The company and director are separate taxpayers with different filings and income records.

Must every director file solely because they are a director?

No. Check the actual personal reporting criteria and any HMRC notice to file.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Record the reason a personal return is needed.
  • Collect payroll and benefits documents.
  • Gather dividend vouchers and payment dates.
  • Identify director loan and company-paid personal items.
  • List other personal income and reliefs.

title: Vinted and eBay: Does Selling Your Own Clothes Mean You Owe Tax?
excerpt: Selling unwanted clothes is not automatically the same as running a resale business. The activity behind the sales matters more than a social-media headline about a fixed number of listings.
metaTitle: Vinted and eBay: Personal Items or Taxable Trading? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Selling online? Distinguish your own used possessions from trading, keep purchase and sale evidence and check valuable-item capital gains separately.
featuredImageAlt: A person sorts used personal clothes for sale while keeping a separate small trading-stock rack, distinction without labels.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Selling goods or services on a digital platform
GOV.UK — Check if you need to tell HMRC about your income from online platforms

content:
Selling unwanted clothes is not automatically the same as running a resale business. The activity behind the sales matters more than a social-media headline about a fixed number of listings.

Separate a clear-out from trading

Describe why you bought the items and what you do now. Selling your own used belongings can be different from regularly buying stock to resell at a profit. If your activity has changed over time, keep the dates clear.

HMRC’s platform guidance says reporting your details does not automatically mean you owe tax. Equally, a lack of a reporting notification does not prove that trading income is outside tax.

Keep evidence before you need it

Save sales summaries, purchase information and explanations of unusual transactions. If you are trading, keep records of associated costs and refunds as well as payouts. Do not delete transaction history simply because an account has closed.

Avoid treating a platform’s reporting threshold as a personal tax allowance. These are different rules and answer different questions.

Ask about valuable items separately

The tax treatment of a valuable possession may need a different review from ordinary trading income. Tell the accountant about high-value sales rather than assuming every personal item is automatically irrelevant.

Example: clearing a wardrobe versus buying stock

Selling clothes you originally bought for yourself is different from regularly sourcing items to resell. Keep enough information to explain the activity, especially if a platform statement shows a large number of transactions.

Is the platform’s reporting threshold a tax allowance?

No. Information-reporting rules and the rules for deciding taxable income serve different purposes. Do not conclude that a particular number of sales automatically makes every receipt taxable, or that staying below a platform-reporting threshold means a business is exempt.

What if I do both activities?

Separate the records of personal-item sales and trading stock, with purchase information where available. Give the accountant an explanation of each rather than subtracting an estimated personal amount from the final bank payouts.

Next step: Use HMRC’s online-income checker. If the activity looks like a business or you are unsure, explain the buying and selling pattern to TaxSimba before deciding whether a return is needed.

Put it into practice

Clearing a wardrobe differs from buying stock

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

Ella sells her own used coats and shoes after a clear-out. Ben buys clothing specifically to resell regularly at a profit. Although both use the same marketplace, the facts are different. Each keeps purchase history, sales and fees so the activity can be explained. A platform reporting transactions to HMRC does not by itself decide that every sale is taxable. Valuable individual possessions can also raise a separate capital-gains question even when the activity is not trading.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Why and how were the items acquired?Distinguish personal use from buying or making items for resale.
Is the activity organised as a trade?Keep the pattern, intention, volume and records for a factual assessment.
Are any valuable possessions involved?Check capital-gains rules separately rather than using the trading allowance for every disposal.

Two more questions you may have

Does platform reporting mean tax is automatically due?

No. Information reporting and tax liability are separate. The nature of the activity and applicable tax rules determine the result.

Does the £1,000 trading allowance apply per platform?

No. Relevant trading income is considered across activities and platforms under the allowance rules, not as a new allowance for each account.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Describe personal use or resale intention.
  • Retain purchase records for significant items.
  • Download sales, refunds and fee statements.
  • Separate personal disposals from trading stock.
  • Flag valuable items for a capital-gains check.

title: Etsy Seller Tax Returns: Why Your Bank Payout Is Not the Whole Record
excerpt: An Etsy payout can combine sales, fees, refunds and adjustments. Preparing a tax return from the final bank deposit alone can make it difficult to understand what the shop earned and spent.
metaTitle: Etsy Seller Tax Returns: Reconcile Sales and Payouts | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare Etsy tax records using gross sales, fees, refunds and payout reconciliations, plus materials, delivery and other business expense evidence.
featuredImageAlt: A handmade-goods seller reconciles marketplace fees, sales records, refunds and bank payouts, products nearby.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Selling goods or services on a digital platform
GOV.UK — Business records if you're self-employed: What records to keep
GOV.UK — Cash basis: Overview

content:
An Etsy payout can combine sales, fees, refunds and adjustments. Preparing a tax return from the final bank deposit alone can make it difficult to understand what the shop earned and spent.

Download the shop statements

Keep transaction exports and relevant payment reports for the tax year. Record which periods they cover and retain supporting invoices. If your shop also sells elsewhere, give the accountant those records rather than assuming one marketplace report covers the whole business.

Reconcile before calculating profit

Ask how the sales figures relate to the payout. Fees deducted before the money reaches your bank need identifying, but should not be deducted again if they have already been accounted for in the figures used.

Refunds and cancelled orders need a clear trail. Keep a note when an adjustment relates to an earlier transaction so it can be considered correctly.

Organise costs by business purpose

Keep evidence for materials, packaging, postage and other shop-related spending. Explain any mixed personal use. The accounting treatment depends on your circumstances and method, not simply the name of the retailer on a receipt.

Platform reporting to HMRC does not replace your responsibility to establish the correct figures and filing position.

Example: the payout reconciliation

A shop may receive customer payments, issue refunds and have fees deducted before the remaining money reaches the bank. Keep a schedule linking those components. Do not treat the final payout and original sales as two separate sets of income.

What if statements use a calendar year?

Tell the accountant what period the export covers. UK tax-year preparation may need a different cut-off, so an annual platform report should not be copied into the return without checking its dates.

Do platform reports mean I no longer need my own records?

No. Your accountant still needs evidence to assess the correct figures and expenses. Download exports and invoices while access is available, and retain explanations for changes such as a shop closure or migration to another sales platform.

Next step: Give TaxSimba your marketplace exports, bank statements and cost records together. This is more useful than sending only the amount withdrawn from the platform.

Put it into practice

The payout is the end of a calculation

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

An Etsy report shows £900 customer sales, £70 refunds and £95 of charges, leaving £735 before any other adjustments. The seller keeps the report and matches the eventual bank transfer rather than recording £735 as the only information. Materials and postage paid elsewhere remain separate costs, with private purchases excluded. She checks transaction dates and any retained balance so sales are not omitted merely because the platform transfers the money in a later period.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
What does each platform deduction represent?Separate fees, refunds and other adjustments using the detailed report.
Do payouts reconcile to the platform balance?Account for timing and retained funds rather than forcing every month to match exactly.
Are stock and other costs supported?Keep purchase records and confirm treatment under the accounting basis used.

Two more questions you may have

Can I claim fees separately after reporting net payouts?

Avoid deducting the same fee twice. Reconcile gross figures and deductions consistently.

Do sales on another platform get a separate allowance?

No. Relevant trading receipts across platforms must be considered together under the applicable rules.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Download detailed sales and adjustment reports.
  • Reconcile opening balance, activity, payouts and closing balance.
  • Keep fee and refund evidence.
  • Gather materials, postage and equipment records.
  • List other selling platforms and cash sales.

title: Airbnb and Holiday-Let Tax Returns After the Furnished Holiday Lettings Changes
excerpt: If you previously treated a property as a furnished holiday letting, do not reuse an old tax calculation without review. The special furnished holiday lettings regime ended for Income Tax from 6 April 2025.
metaTitle: Airbnb and Holiday Let Tax 2025/26: What Changed? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare Airbnb and holiday-let tax records after the Furnished Holiday Lettings regime ended: gross bookings, platform fees, ownership and transition records.
featuredImageAlt: A holiday-let host reviews property records and dated occupancy planner with adviser, small seaside cottage visible.

sources.label: GOV.UK — PIM4165 - Repeal of Furnished Holiday Lettings rules : Overview - HMRC internal manual
GOV.UK — Work out your rental income when you let property
GOV.UK — Check if you need to tell HMRC about your income from online platforms

content:
If you previously treated a property as a furnished holiday letting, do not reuse an old tax calculation without review. The special furnished holiday lettings regime ended for Income Tax from 6 April 2025.

Tell the accountant how the property is used

Explain whether you let a room in your home, a whole property or several properties. Include ownership details, personal use and the dates of lettings. Short stays do not, by themselves, establish that the previous special rules continue.

Keep platform and property records together

Download booking statements showing amounts charged, fees, refunds and payouts. Keep invoices for property costs and identify spending that improves the property rather than simply maintains it. The accountant needs to review the substance of the work.

If you had prior-year losses, allowances or other carry-forward figures, provide the earlier return and calculations. These should not be guessed from the latest platform balance.

Check the scope of the service

Tell the accountant about overseas property, shared ownership or substantial services to guests. Different facts can require more work than an ordinary rental return, so agree the service before purchasing.

Example: the first year after the old regime

For an individual’s 2025/26 return, do not simply copy a prior-year furnished holiday lettings calculation. Bring it to the accountant as background, together with current records and details of any carry-forward figures.

Does using Airbnb make the letting tax-free?

No. A booking platform does not decide the tax treatment. Letting a furnished room in your home, operating a whole-property holiday let and providing substantial services can raise different questions.

Should I deduct the platform fee twice?

No. Check how the figures were assembled. If the statement shows net payouts, the accountant may need the gross booking and fee breakdown. Keep refunds, cancellations and personal-use periods identifiable so the final records reflect what actually happened.

Next step: Ask TaxSimba to review your letting arrangement and the relevant tax year. Bring the previous treatment as background, rather than assuming it remains correct after the rule change.

Put it into practice

Old holiday-let treatment should not roll forward unchecked

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A holiday-let owner preparing 2025/26 brings the prior year's accounts, booking reports and records of losses and allowances. She reconciles gross bookings to fees, refunds and payouts, then asks the accountant to check the transition from the former Furnished Holiday Lettings regime. She does not copy last year's tax treatment merely because the same property is still advertised online. Finance costs, carried-forward items and private use need checking under the rules for the new year.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Which tax year is being prepared?Separate the former regime's years from the post-abolition property-income treatment.
Are historical losses and allowances documented?Bring prior computations so transitional treatment can be checked.
Does the booking income reconcile?Supply gross bookings, cancellations, fees, payouts and private-use details.

Two more questions you may have

Does listing on Airbnb determine the tax regime?

No. The property's facts and the law for the relevant year matter; a platform label does not preserve the former FHL rules.

Can I discard the old computations after the change?

No. Earlier losses, allowances and asset history may still matter. Keep them with the new year's property records.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Identify ownership and the tax year.
  • Collect prior FHL computations and carry-forward schedules.
  • Reconcile gross bookings, refunds, fees and payouts.
  • Record private use and property expenditure.
  • Flag finance costs and assets for transition review.

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Joint Rental Property on a Tax Return: Do Both Owners Report the Same Amount?
excerpt: Joint owners should not assume they can choose any rental-income split or that one owner’s return settles the other’s position. The ownership and relationship between the owners need to be understood first.
metaTitle: Joint Rental Property Tax Returns: Check Each Share | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare joint-property tax figures using ownership evidence, gross rent, shared costs and each owner's personal return rather than copying the same totals.
featuredImageAlt: Joint landlords compare their actual ownership records and individual income folders with an accountant.

sources.label: GOV.UK — PIM1035 - Introduction: Jointly owned property and partnerships - HMRC internal manual
GOV.UK — Work out your rental income when you let property

content:
Joint owners should not assume they can choose any rental-income split or that one owner’s return settles the other’s position. The ownership and relationship between the owners need to be understood first.

Explain who owns what

Give the accountant the ownership documents and describe how income has been reported previously. Spouses and civil partners can be subject to rules that differ from those applying to other co-owners. A relevant declaration may need formal evidence and timing requirements.

Do not change the reported split merely because one person pays the mortgage or receives the rent. Those facts need consideration, but do not replace a proper review.

Share the full property statement

Provide total rent, letting-agent deductions and expense evidence, then explain the amount you believe belongs to you. This allows the accountant to reconcile the property rather than relying on a single net figure.

If separate accountants handle each owner, make sure the underlying figures and assumptions are consistent. Otherwise the two returns may describe the same property differently.

Keep the engagement individual

Ask whether the purchased service covers one owner or both. Authorisations, approvals and tax payments belong to the relevant client, even where the property records overlap.

Example: rent paid into one owner’s account

The payment destination is useful evidence but does not, on its own, settle the share taxable on each owner. Give the accountant the ownership information and explain the arrangement behind the payment.

Do spouses and unrelated owners always use the same rules?

No. The relationship between owners and relevant ownership evidence can affect the treatment. Obtain advice on the actual arrangement instead of copying the split used by another landlord.

How do we prevent inconsistent returns?

Share the same complete property statement with the accountants concerned and identify the assumptions used for each person’s share. Keep a record of changes. If an error is discovered later, make sure the affected people know which figures need reviewing.

Next step: Send TaxSimba the ownership information and complete rental statements so your share can be checked before the return is prepared.

Put it into practice

The agent's total is not each owner's total

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

Two siblings receive one agent statement showing £20,000 gross rent. They provide the ownership agreement and details of their income-sharing arrangement so the accountant can establish what each should report. They reconcile shared expenses to the same source documents and retain a schedule explaining the allocation. If one pays an invoice personally, that bank payment alone does not settle the tax split. Married couples and civil partners living together need their specific rules checked separately.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Who owns the beneficial interest?Keep the ownership and income-allocation evidence, including relevant changes.
Do special spouse or civil-partner rules apply?Check the applicable default and any valid declaration rather than choosing an arbitrary split.
Can each person's figures be reconciled?Allocate income and costs consistently and retain the workings for both returns.

Two more questions you may have

Do both owners report the full property's rent?

No. Establish the correct allocation for each person; duplicating the entire rent would misstate the personal returns.

Does paying all the mortgage change the ownership split?

Not automatically. Provide the ownership and borrowing arrangements for review rather than inferring tax shares from bank payments alone.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Collect ownership and beneficial-interest documents.
  • Record any relevant declarations and changes.
  • Prepare full gross rent and cost schedules.
  • Document the allocation to each owner.
  • Reconcile each person's return pack to the shared records.

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

query: joint rental property tax returns  check each share
answer: Joint owners should not assume they can choose any rental-income split or that one owner’s return settles the other’s position. The ownership and relationship between the owners need to be understood first.
alt: Joint landlords compare their actual ownership records and individual income folders with an accountant.
details: Keep the ownership and income-allocation evidence, including relevant changes.
Check the applicable default and any valid declaration rather than choosing an arbitrary split.
Allocate income and costs consistently and retain the workings for both returns.
checklist: Who owns the beneficial interest?
Do special spouse or civil-partner rules apply?
Can each person's figures be reconciled?

depth.exampleTitle: The agent's total is not each owner's total
example: Two siblings receive one agent statement showing £20,000 gross rent. They provide the ownership agreement and details of their income-sharing arrangement so the accountant can establish what each should report. They reconcile shared expenses to the same source documents and retain a schedule explaining the allocation. If one pays an invoice personally, that bank payment alone does not settle the tax split. Married couples and civil partners living together need their specific rules checked separately.

questions: Do both owners report the full property's rent?
No. Establish the correct allocation for each person; duplicating the entire rent would misstate the personal returns.
Does paying all the mortgage change the ownership split?
Not automatically. Provide the ownership and borrowing arrangements for review rather than inferring tax shares from bank payments alone.
